title: Personal portrait — professional motivations and preferences
scenario: Working hypothesis: extensive automation of some knowledge work tasks between 2026 and 2036. This scenario is not presented as a certain forecast.
notice: An exploratory questionnaire that has not been scientifically validated. It describes stated preferences, not measured skills, a standardised personality assessment or a tool for recruitment. These suggestions do not predict job loss or the success of a career change.

answerLabels.ne_sais_pas: I do not know / not applicable

q001.prompt: I enjoy understanding the root causes of a problem before looking for a solution.

q002.prompt: I enjoy understanding how different parts of a system influence each other.

q003.prompt: I willingly check claims rather than relying on consensus.

q004.prompt: I prefer a good enough, usable solution to an ideal one that is difficult to finish.

q005.prompt: I can move forward with a project even when some information is still missing.

q006.prompt: I am interested in comparing several scenarios and anticipating their consequences.

q007.prompt: I naturally think about the indirect and long-term effects of a decision.

q008.prompt: I appreciate being challenged with sound arguments and evidence.

q009.prompt: Inconsistencies and imprecise details bother me, even when they seem minor.

q010.prompt: I prefer thinking about concepts to putting them into practice.

q011.prompt: I often imagine new ideas, projects or ways of doing things.

q012.prompt: Turning an idea into something tangible gives me a great deal of satisfaction.

q013.prompt: The appearance, design or aesthetics of a result matter a lot to me.

q014.prompt: I enjoy refining a result until it reaches a high standard of quality.

q015.prompt: Which stages of a project do you enjoy most? Choose up to two answers.

options.imaginer: Imagining the idea and exploring possibilities
options.concevoir: Designing the structure and how it works
options.construire: Building something tangible and solving problems
options.impact: Seeing the effects on the people who use it
options.organiser: Organising the project and coordinating its stages

q016.prompt: I enjoy starting a new project, even when its outcome is uncertain.

q017.prompt: The difficulties I encounter while working on a project motivate me.

q018.prompt: I enjoy telling stories, creating content or finding original forms of expression.

q019.prompt: I often prioritise a first working version that I can improve later.

q020.prompt: I can stay motivated by maintaining and refining a creation that is already finished.

q021.prompt: I spontaneously explore a wide range of subjects unrelated to my main activity.

q022.prompt: I am comfortable learning on my own using resources I choose myself.

q023.prompt: I enjoy studying a subject until I understand its mechanisms in detail.

q024.prompt: I need to discover new subjects or types of projects regularly.

q025.prompt: To learn, I prefer trying things in practice to only reading or listening.

q026.prompt: I willingly spend free time understanding something that intrigues me.

q027.prompt: Becoming a recognised expert in a specific field appeals to me.

q028.prompt: I try to understand why a method works, not just how to apply it.

q029.prompt: I prefer studying the same subjects for years to frequently discovering new ones.

q030.prompt: Learning new skills on my own gives me satisfaction.

q031.prompt: I prefer deciding on my own working methods.

q032.prompt: I like working with explicit goals and a sufficiently defined framework.

q033.prompt: Frequent interruptions significantly reduce my satisfaction at work.

q034.prompt: Tight deadlines and urgency motivate me.

q035.prompt: I can enjoy work that involves many repetitive tasks.

q036.prompt: I find it difficult when someone supervises every action I take in detail.

q037.prompt: I can work effectively without a prior plan or defined organisation.

q038.prompt: I prefer spending a long time on one task to juggling several requests.

q039.prompt: When priorities change frequently, I remain energetic and calm.

q040.prompt: I enjoy taking a project from its initial definition to the final result.

q041.prompt: After a day full of social interaction, I need quiet and solitude.

q042.prompt: Meeting new people at a social gathering usually gives me energy.

q043.prompt: I prefer an in-depth conversation with one person to a large group discussion.

q044.prompt: I enjoy presenting my ideas to an audience when I know the subject well.

q045.prompt: I need to talk or collaborate with other people several times a day.

q046.prompt: I regularly choose to spend time alone to recharge.

q047.prompt: I enjoy explaining ideas or passing on knowledge.

q048.prompt: Helping someone directly to make progress gives me satisfaction.

q049.prompt: I prefer making important decisions collectively rather than individually.

q050.prompt: I generally feel comfortable starting a conversation with strangers.

q051.prompt: I find hierarchical decisions difficult to accept when they are not explained or justified.

q052.prompt: When I disagree, I try to defend my point of view with arguments.

q053.prompt: Managing a team and following other people’s work interests me.

q054.prompt: When working with others, I prefer giving them considerable freedom over their methods.

q055.prompt: Feeling respected and appreciated at work is essential for my long-term commitment.

q056.prompt: I can set a clear boundary when someone does not honour their commitments.

q057.prompt: I would prefer having line-management responsibility for a team to an expert role without management.

q058.prompt: I can easily follow an instruction even when it seems arbitrary to me.

q059.prompt: I avoid defending my disagreement if it might create tension in a relationship.

q060.prompt: I enjoy supporting someone’s learning and development.

q061.prompt: I enjoy contacting strangers to offer them a product or service.

q062.prompt: Persuading someone to buy a product or service motivates me.

q063.prompt: I enjoy negotiating prices or contracts in a professional setting.

q064.prompt: Starting and developing my own business appeals to me.

q065.prompt: I am willing to accept irregular income for a long period to develop a project.

q066.prompt: Occasional, playful negotiation without significant professional stakes can be fun for me.

q067.prompt: I would enjoy spending a substantial part of my time on customer relationships and sales.

q068.prompt: I prefer creating a product whose sales can work with little personal involvement in selling.

q069.prompt: Actively looking for new customers, partners or contracts interests me.

q070.prompt: I would generally prioritise a fixed income over a potentially higher-paying but highly uncertain opportunity.

q071.prompt: Being free to decide how I use my time is one of my main goals in life.

q072.prompt: Having predictable, regular income is very important to my well-being.

q073.prompt: Being recognised for the quality of my work is a powerful motivation for me.

q074.prompt: I want my work to bring a tangible benefit to other people.

q075.prompt: I would prefer mainly manual or physical work to mainly intellectual work.

q076.prompt: Being able to work remotely is an important benefit for me.

q078.prompt: I can stay on the same project for several years if I get along with the people and continue to make progress.

q079.prompt: I would be willing to accept less intellectually stimulating work if it gave me much more control over my time.

q080.prompt: Which of these goals would matter most in the long term? Choose up to two answers.

options.revenus: Reaching a high level of income
options.creer: Imagining and building my own projects
options.apprendre: Continuing to learn and solve problems
options.impact: Having a positive impact on others
options.liberte_geo: Choosing where I work and travel

socle_financier.title: Review your financial security
socle_financier.summary: Understand how dependent you are on income from work and identify room to manoeuvre before taking risks.
steps: Calculate the monthly cost of essential expenses.
Identify genuinely guaranteed income and unavoidable outgoings.
Set a gradual target for an accessible reserve in case income falls.
socle_financier.caveat: The questionnaire does not collect income, savings, debts or family constraints, so it cannot assess your actual financial security.

apprendre_ia.title: Learn to use AI in real professional situations
apprendre_ia.summary: Use, check and integrate AI systems to solve practical problems beyond writing prompts.
steps: Choose a real, time-consuming task in your work.
Test an automation with human oversight and measure errors.
Document what works, what fails and the time actually saved.
apprendre_ia.caveat: Knowing how to use AI tools does not in itself protect your job.

reasons.apprendre_ia-r4: Prioritising usable solutions and practical trials

fiabiliser_automatisation.title: Specialise in the reliability of automated systems
fiabiliser_automatisation.summary: Learn to evaluate, secure, monitor and correct processes where AI can make mistakes.
steps: Learn the principles of testing, evaluating and monitoring AI systems.
Set up a small, monitored automation and failure scenarios.
Make results verifiable and explain the limitations.
fiabiliser_automatisation.caveat: This speciality remains exposed to automation and requires technical skills you may need to acquire.

reasons.fiabiliser_automatisation-r3: Refining details and seeking high quality
reasons.fiabiliser_automatisation-r4: Understanding a subject’s mechanisms in detail

expertise_metier.title: Build solid expertise in an economic sector
expertise_metier.summary: Understand the constraints of an occupation or sector in depth to create value beyond an interchangeable task.
steps: Choose a concrete sector with identifiable problems and budgets.
Talk to three professionals about their everyday constraints.
Map its processes, errors and recurring needs.
expertise_metier.caveat: Sector expertise is not a guarantee; its value also depends on access to real situations and demand.

reasons.expertise_metier-r1: Understanding a subject’s mechanisms in detail
reasons.expertise_metier-r4: Imagining staying on the same project for several years

preuves_resultats.title: Move towards work with responsibility for outcomes
preuves_resultats.summary: Connect your work to useful, measurable outcomes rather than only completing tasks.
steps: Choose a problem with measurable effects.
Define an indicator before taking action.
Present a real case: problem, decision, result and limitations.
preuves_resultats.caveat: Roles with responsibility can also change with AI; no position is guaranteed.

reasons.preuves_resultats-r1: Taking a project from definition to completion
reasons.preuves_resultats-r2: Wanting to bring a tangible benefit to others
reasons.preuves_resultats-r3: Prioritising usable solutions and practical trials

montrer_travail.title: Build a portfolio of professional evidence
montrer_travail.summary: Make your ability to solve real problems visible through verifiable results.
steps: Document two recent projects without disclosing confidential data.
For each, present the situation, approach and observable impact.
Collect these cases on a professional page that is easy to share.
montrer_travail.caveat: A portfolio increases visibility but does not create jobs if demand collapses.

reasons.montrer_travail-r1: Being motivated by recognition for work
reasons.montrer_travail-r3: Refining details and seeking high quality
reasons.montrer_travail-r4: Enjoying presenting and passing on ideas

reconversion_progressive.title: Prepare a gradual, reversible career change
reconversion_progressive.summary: Explore another sector or role without giving up your current income too early.
steps: List two sectors accessible through transferable skills.
Try a short course, work observation or a pilot project.
Compare the reality of the occupation with your personal constraints before switching.
reconversion_progressive.caveat: The questionnaire does not know your degrees, qualifications or local opportunities.

hybride_materiel.title: Develop skills connecting software and the physical world
hybride_materiel.summary: Explore real technical systems: instrumentation, maintenance, home automation or on-site automation.
steps: Choose an introduction to home automation, sensors or maintenance.
Build or observe a tangible physical device.
Check entry requirements: training, authorisations and presence on site.
hybride_materiel.caveat: Work tied to the physical world can also be affected by AI and often requires travel.

reasons.hybride_materiel-r3: Being drawn to manual or physical work

activite_terrain.title: Explore a service occupation rooted in the physical world
activite_terrain.summary: Evaluate local activities where places, equipment and people are central.
steps: Observe two hands-on occupations and their real constraints.
Learn about qualifications, physical demands and possible income.
Test your actual interest before starting a lengthy career change.
activite_terrain.caveat: Physical strain, regulatory obligations and access to a local market are not measured.

reasons.activite_terrain-r1: Being drawn to manual or physical work
reasons.activite_terrain-r3: Finding satisfaction in helping someone progress

cautions.activite_terrain-c1: You stated little interest in manual work: do not choose this path without a practical trial.

transmission_formation.title: Experiment with teaching or practical training
transmission_formation.summary: Turn useful experience into workshops, support or learning resources.
steps: Choose a subject you genuinely know.
Try a short workshop with a few participants.
Gather feedback and check whether there is paying demand.
transmission_formation.caveat: Generic educational content can face strong competition from AI.

reasons.transmission_formation-r1: Enjoying presenting and passing on ideas
reasons.transmission_formation-r2: Finding satisfaction in helping someone progress
reasons.transmission_formation-r3: Wanting to bring a tangible benefit to others
reasons.transmission_formation-r4: Understanding a subject’s mechanisms in detail

microproduit_recurrent.title: Test a product that generates recurring revenue
microproduit_recurrent.summary: Build a useful product or service for several customers without selling every hour of your work.
steps: Identify a concrete problem that someone already pays to solve.
Talk to five potential customers before developing anything.
Test a minimal offer alongside stable income if necessary.
microproduit_recurrent.caveat: A product does not ensure automatic sales; acquisition, support, competition and costs still matter.

reasons.microproduit_recurrent-r1: Being drawn to starting and developing a business
reasons.microproduit_recurrent-r3: Choosing methods with little detailed supervision
reasons.microproduit_recurrent-r4: Making control over time a priority

cautions.microproduit_recurrent-c1: Given your need for stability, test this project alongside a reliable source of income.
cautions.microproduit_recurrent-c2: Limited enthusiasm for selling makes an appropriate acquisition approach or a partner essential.

service_packagé.title: Create a standardised service offer
service_packagé.summary: Define a clear, repeatable service priced for its value rather than the time spent.
steps: Identify a recurring problem for a specific audience.
Define an offer with deliverables, timescale, price and boundaries.
Test selling it before automating delivery.
service_packagé.caveat: Prospecting and customer acquisition remain necessary even for a standardised service.

reasons.service_packagé-r1: Being drawn to starting and developing a business
reasons.service_packagé-r2: Prioritising usable solutions and practical trials
reasons.service_packagé-r3: Appreciating defined goals and a clear framework

partenariat_complementaire.title: Find a partner with complementary commercial skills
partenariat_complementaire.summary: Work with a sector or sales specialist on a limited basis to separate production from market access.
steps: List the complementary resources you need: customers, sector knowledge or distribution.
Test a collaboration on a short project.
Clarify contributions, revenue and exit rules in writing before a lasting partnership.
partenariat_complementaire.caveat: A partnership does not remove commercial risk and can create dependence on a relationship.

reasons.partenariat_complementaire-r1: Being drawn to starting and developing a business
reasons.partenariat_complementaire-r2: Being less drawn to customer prospecting
reasons.partenariat_complementaire-r3: Being less drawn to direct selling
reasons.partenariat_complementaire-r6: Reporting willingness to defend a view despite possible tension

cautions.partenariat_complementaire-c1: Prioritise a small collaboration and structured exchanges rather than a group with constant social demands.

diagnostic_conseil.title: Test limited diagnostic or consulting assignments
diagnostic_conseil.summary: Offer an analysis or audit focused on a specific problem with understandable deliverables.
steps: Select a type of problem you know and can verify.
Create an audit framework and an anonymised example.
Test a first assignment with limited scope and explicit goals.
diagnostic_conseil.caveat: Consulting requires finding customers and building credibility.

reasons.diagnostic_conseil-r3: Understanding a subject’s mechanisms in detail

audience_ciblee.title: Develop a focused professional audience
audience_ciblee.summary: Share analysis and real experience to build trust and visibility with a specific audience.
steps: Choose a specific audience and a useful subject.
Publish four pieces based on verifiable experience.
Observe the quality of exchanges before increasing your publishing pace.
audience_ciblee.caveat: An audience guarantees neither income nor job protection; content creation can itself be automated.

reasons.audience_ciblee-r1: Enjoying presenting and passing on ideas
reasons.audience_ciblee-r2: Creating content or original forms of expression
reasons.audience_ciblee-r3: Being motivated by recognition for work
reasons.audience_ciblee-r4: Understanding a subject’s mechanisms in detail

cautions.audience_ciblee-c1: Prepared, asynchronous content may suit you better than continuous social interaction.

reseau_confiance.title: Maintain a small network of trusted relationships
reseau_confiance.summary: Strengthen lasting professional connections to access opportunities and information that are hard to obtain through applications alone.
steps: Reconnect with three people whose work you know.
Share practical help or a resource without immediately asking for anything.
Maintain these relationships at a realistic pace.
reseau_confiance.caveat: A network alone cannot compensate for a substantial contraction in the market.

reasons.reseau_confiance-r1: Placing great importance on respect and appreciation
reasons.reseau_confiance-r3: Preferring quiet and limited interaction to recharge
reasons.reseau_confiance-r4: Seeking justified decisions and horizontal relationships

canal_independant.title: Create a contact channel independent of platforms
canal_independant.summary: Gradually build a list of subscribers or customers who choose to receive your content and offers.
steps: Choose a useful theme and editorial promise.
Create a voluntary subscription channel that is easy to leave.
Publish regularly, then evaluate subscriptions and feedback.
canal_independant.caveat: A subscriber list is not automatically a profitable asset; trust and consistency matter.

reasons.canal_independant-r1: Enjoying presenting and passing on ideas
reasons.canal_independant-r2: Choosing methods with little detailed supervision
reasons.canal_independant-r3: Imagining staying on the same project for several years
reasons.canal_independant-r4: Being drawn to starting and developing a business

collectif_projets.title: Join a small group with complementary projects
collectif_projets.summary: Share some opportunities and skills without carrying every function of a business on your own.
steps: Identify two professionals with complementary skills.
Try a project with a limited timescale.
Define responsibilities and how decisions will be made.
collectif_projets.caveat: Collaboration can add coordination and interpersonal risk without producing income.

reasons.collectif_projets-r2: Seeking justified decisions and horizontal relationships
reasons.collectif_projets-r3: Giving others freedom over their methods
reasons.collectif_projets-r4: Wanting to bring a tangible benefit to others

maintien_employabilite.title: Keep several employment and training options open
maintien_employabilite.summary: Monitor changes in occupations close to yours and maintain recent evidence of transferable skills.
steps: List three related roles and the skills they share.
Identify skills gaps and work on one at a time.
Update evidence of your work and maintain your network.
maintien_employabilite.caveat: This strategy improves your ability to recover from setbacks without guaranteeing recruitment.

reasons.maintien_employabilite-r3: Prioritising usable solutions and practical trials
reasons.maintien_employabilite-r4: Placing great importance on predictable income

patrimoine_diversifie.title: Learn about diversified savings and assets
patrimoine_diversifie.summary: Gradually reduce dependence on a salary by understanding emergency savings, diversification and investment risks.
steps: Review essential expenses, debts and available savings.
Understand the difference between emergency savings and long-term investment.
Study diversification suited to your situation before making decisions.
patrimoine_diversifie.caveat: Investments can lose value and access to capital is not guaranteed.

reasons.patrimoine_diversifie-r1: Making control over time a priority
reasons.patrimoine_diversifie-r2: Placing great importance on predictable income
reasons.patrimoine_diversifie-r3: Preferring to limit urgency and frequent change

adapter_charges.title: Reduce fixed expenses and gain flexibility
adapter_charges.summary: Lower unavoidable expenses to widen your options if your professional situation changes.
steps: Calculate fixed expenses over three months.
Identify one or two costs you could reduce without greatly harming daily life.
Put the savings into an accessible reserve.
adapter_charges.caveat: The scope for saving depends on your real situation, which the questionnaire does not collect.

reasons.adapter_charges-r1: Placing great importance on predictable income
reasons.adapter_charges-r3: Making control over time a priority

activite_accompagnement.title: Explore work centred on supporting people
activite_accompagnement.summary: Test work in which listening, relationships and practical help play an important role.
steps: Observe a real activity that supports people.
Check any training and obligations involved.
Test the pace of interpersonal interaction before planning a career change.
activite_accompagnement.caveat: Supporting people is not necessarily protected from changes associated with AI.

reasons.activite_accompagnement-r1: Finding satisfaction in helping someone progress
reasons.activite_accompagnement-r3: Wanting to bring a tangible benefit to others
reasons.activite_accompagnement-r4: Reporting ease in talking to strangers

conception_produit.title: Develop product design and user experience skills
conception_produit.summary: Move closer to key decisions: whom to serve, which problem to solve, which outcome to measure and which constraints to respect.
steps: Analyse a user journey in your sector.
Identify a recurring problem and propose a concrete improvement.
Test the improvement with real users and measure its effect.
conception_produit.caveat: Product design is not immune to AI; expertise must be demonstrated in practice.

reasons.conception_produit-r3: Wanting to bring a tangible benefit to others
reasons.conception_produit-r4: Giving importance to design and appearance
